newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end sharply lower, off session lows.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end sharply lower, off session lows.

text.p: Share prices in Madrid ended sharply lower but off lows on Monday, catching up after Wall Street slumped on Friday during a public holiday here.

Dealers said the Dow's shaky performance has been adding to volatility in a thin and trading-based market, but the prospect of further retracement in Spain was not particularly unsettling as the market has been sharply overvalued.
The general index fell 13.43 points, 2.28 percent, to 576.02 and the Ibex-35 shed 156.36 points, 2.33 percent, to 6,552.15.
BBV, one of this year's best performers, shed 145 pesetas, 3.49 percent, to 4,015 pesetas.

"To me (the fall) is more disinterest than negative feeling. Our next (Ibex) support is 6,470 and it won't be until we get to that level that we'll see domestic funds coming back in. But I think foreign final investors may wait even for 6,200," said a trader at Credit Lyonnais Securities.

With domestic news --corporate or economic-- very thin on the ground, the market's margin to fall or rise is likely to continue to hinge on the performance of foreign markets, and in particular this week's rate decisions by the German and U.S. monetary authorities.
